hypothesis: Treating a recovery build's canonical active-runtime timeout as a retryable preserved-work outcome, constructing one stable recovery payload, retaining explicitly keyed queued work across runtime recovery, and requiring explicit retry lineage before dead-letter supersession will prevent stranded builder work without allowing unrelated successes to erase failure evidence.

metricsCompared.name: active-runtime timeout continuation
metricsCompared.baseline: zero recovery requests after the cited recovery build exhausted active runtime
metricsCompared.candidate: one explicit idempotency-keyed recovery request with preserved-work review evidence

metricsCompared.name: dead-letter lineage accuracy
metricsCompared.baseline: an unrelated later builder success dismissed the cited timeout dead letter
metricsCompared.candidate: unrelated success leaves the dead letter open; only a linked successful retry dismisses it

metricsCompared.name: restart replay durability
metricsCompared.baseline: runtime recovery evicted the accepted keyed continuation while a differently described scan replay was rejected
metricsCompared.candidate: the scan emits the canonical payload as a replay and the retained keyed continuation executes after runtime.recovered

rationale: The candidate preserves the existing bounded recovery shape, keeps durable keyed work behind the prepended runtime reset, and narrows automatic dead-letter cleanup to explicit causal lineage. Focused finalizer, runtime restart/replay, active-timeout, dead-letter supersession, and successful continuation fixtures cover the cited regression without adding another scheduler or bypassing claim/worktree cleanup.
